data.title: Euro zone bond yields drop as investors seek safety from AI-trade rout
data.description:
(Updates throughout)

* Bond markets are watching oil and the economy as well as equities

* Analyst says bond market move has been relatively modest so far

* Oil prices eased on Friday, boosting bond yields

By Javi West Larrañaga

GDANSK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Euro zone bond yields fell on Friday as global stocks slid on doubts about the AI sector, sending investors towards safe-haven government debt.

Anthropic shares jumped in the company's blockbuster IPO on Thursday but did not revive excitement around AI stocks more broadly and the stock fell by as much as 10% on Friday.

The negative equities mood benefited safe-haven German bonds, the euro area benchmark, sending 10-year yields down 11 basis points to 3.295%, their biggest daily fall since April. .

Two-year yields, which are more sensitive to central bank rate expectations, also fell 10 bps to 3.059%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Lyn Graham-Taylor, a senior rates strategist at Rabobank, said risk-off moves could have been larger, given the extent of the equities retreat.

"It's quite a decent move in bond yields, but you could argue that it's not particularly massive for some of the equity declines we've seen," he said.

French and Italian bonds also picked up, with yields down around 7 bps.

The spread between French and German 10-year bond yields - which has risen sharply this year - widened by almost 5 bps to 158 bps.

Euro zone bond yields have fallen from multiyear or multidecade highs in September and October as energy prices have cooled and tech stocks have dropped.

As the mood on equities markets remained broadly negative, European stocks dropped and Asian equities had their worst week since March. The US' S&P 500 was on track for its sixth consecutive loss, its longest losing streak since April 2024.

Graham-Taylor said it was too soon to say whether the AI selloff would bring an extended period of strength for bonds, as markets were also watching oil prices and the economy.

Oil prices fell on Friday, also boosting bonds, with Brent crude futures dropping 1% to $91 a barrel, down sharply from $118 a barrel in late October.

On the macro front, official European Commission data on Friday showed euro zone consumer confidence improved month-on-month in November, defying the decline expected by economists.

Earlier in the day, ECB President Christine Lagarde said the European Central Bank will make its currency swap lines with other countries more accessible to shield the euro area from outside financial shocks and boost the euro's global role.

(Reporting by Harry Robertson in London and Javi West Larrañaga in Gdansk; Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria, Sharon Singleton and Barbara Lewis)

* Markets await Lula's pick for finance minister
    * BofA sees scope for renewed capital inflows into Brazil
    * Mexican retail sales signal softer domestic demand

    By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
       Nov 20 (Reuters) - Latin American equities fell to over
one-year lows on Friday as a global equity selloff intensified
after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore confidence in the AI
sector, while prospects of higher US interest rates kept
pressure on regional currencies.
    While Latin American markets have limited direct exposure to
the technology sector, the deterioration in global risk
sentiment spilled over into the region.
    MSCI's index of Latin American equities fell
0.86% and was on track for its lowest weekly decline since
November 2025, while the corresponding currency gauge
 fell 1.5% and was on track for its fourth
consecutive weekly loss.
    Brazil's benchmark Bovespa index, which accounts for
the largest weighting in the MSCI Latin America index, fell
0.69%, pressured by losses in heavyweight energy stocks.
    Investor also monitored domestic developments. Brazilian
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is nearing a decision on his
next finance minister, with an announcement possible as early as
next week, according to six sources familiar with the
discussions.
    The Brazilian real was down 0.24% against the US
dollar.
    "Gains in the Brazilian real were only fleeting, with
investors still wary that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
has no interest in fiscal consolidation," said Chris Turner,
global head of markets research at ING.​‌
    Separately, Bank of America said there remains a potential
path for capital inflows to return to Latin America's largest
economy despite a challenging economic environment at home and
abroad.

    MEXICO TRADE HOPES RISE; COMMODITIES RETREAT
    In Mexico, the peso was up 0.29%. Investors took note of a
potentially positive development on the trade front as EU
agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen said he expects
Mexico to clear the final hurdle for a new EU trade pact to take
effect by the end of the year, bringing Mexican and European
interests closer together.
    Meanwhile, Mexican retail sales fell in September from the
previous month, data from the national statistics agency showed,
pointing to softer consumer demand despite remaining higher than
a year ago.
    Broader global factors also weighed on sentiment. Commodity
prices fell, with gold down 2% and copper was headed for
its biggest weekly drop in 19 months.
    Chile's peso fell 0.29% against the dollar, while
Peru's sol slipped 0.15%.​‌
    Brent crude fell around 1% as concerns over supply
disruptions eased, with exports from the Middle East remaining
resilient despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital,
Riyadh, and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of
Hormuz.

data.title: BJ's Raises Full-Year Earnings Outlook; Promotional Activities Weigh on Merchandise Margins
data.description:
11:13 AM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings (BJ) raised its full-year earnings outlook on Friday after better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results, although the warehouse club operator's merchandise margin contracted amid heavier promotional activity.

The company lifted its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $5.10 to $5.30 from $4.60 to $4.80. It now expects comparable club sales excluding gasoline to grow 2.5% to 3%, compared with 2% to 3% previously.

The FactSet-polled consensus is for non-GAAP EPS of $4.74 and comparable sales growth of 2.6%.

Shares of the company fell 2.8% in Friday trade, reducing their year-to-date gain to about 20%.

BJ's merchandise gross margin rate, which excludes gasoline sales and membership fee income, declined by 170 basis points year over year for the quarter ended October, primarily due to promotional activities associated with its 42nd birthday celebration.

The decline reflected an estimated $56 million in one-time promotional expenses, Chief Financial Officer Laura Felice said during an earnings call, according to a FactSet transcript.

BJ's recognized a one-time pretax benefit of around $240 million in the quarter after resolving litigation over credit card interchange fees in which it was the plaintiff. The company used the settlement benefit to invest in its stakeholders, Chief Executive Bob Eddy said on the call.

As part of its birthday celebration, BJ's offered discounts of 42% on featured products during a nearly six-week promotional event. Comparable club traffic increased 6% year over year during the promotion, Eddy said.

The warehouse club operator's adjusted EPS rose to $1.73 from $1.16 the year before, exceeding the Street's view for $1.26. The results benefited from the litigation settlement, partially offset by investments made during the quarter, Felice said.

Overall revenue advanced nearly 18% to $6.28 billion, ahead of the average analyst estimate of $5.97 billion. Comparable club sales, excluding gasoline, rose 4.1% and were ahead of the market's forecast for a rise of 2.9%.

BJ's was positioned to gain from shoppers switching to warehouse clubs in the third quarter as consumers tried to stretch their budgets amid a tough economy, UBS Securities said in a note last week. The brokerage had projected comparable sales excluding fuel to rise 3% and adjusted EPS of $1.28.

"We're pleased with how the third quarter came together and we enter the holiday season with a clear plan and a strong foundation," Felice said on the call.

Walmart ( WMT ) raised its full-year financial outlook on Thursday, although the retail giant's fiscal third-quarter comparable sales growth in the US fell short of Wall Street's expectations. Target ( TGT ) lifted its full-year sales outlook earlier in the week as its fiscal third-quarter comparable sales grew more than market expectations.

Warehouse chain Costco Wholesale ( COST ) is scheduled to release its latest financial results next month.

data.title: Bessent advocates lower Fed rate hike, cites energy shock
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the Federal Reserve to not embrace a big interest rate hike as some Fed governors are doing, citing the energy supply shock and a drop in crude delivery prices.

Bessent said in an interview with CNBC that one governor who is backing 50 basis point hike had wanted a similar cut within the last year. "So it seems somewhat peripatetic to now want a the bigger hike just 12 months or 11 months later," he said. "So I would encourage the Fed to look forward, not backwards."

(Reporting by Doina Chiacu; Editing by Katharine Jackson)

data.title: National Advertising Division Found Shark Supported “More Features” Claim; Recommended Incentivized Reviews be Discontinued
data.description:
New York, NY, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- In a challenge brought by Dyson, Inc., BBB National Programs’ National Advertising Division determined that SharkNinja Operating, LLC supported its “More Features Half the Price” claim, found that Shark’s tagline “When Air Just Isn’t Enough,” standing alone, does not convey an objective or comparative message, and recommended that Shark discontinue two incentivized consumer reviews describing drying and straightening in “one step.”

Shark markets a range of home and personal-care products, including the SilkiPro Straight Hair Straightener and Dryer, a wet-to-dry styling tool that combines heated airflow, ceramic plates, and interchangeable combs. Dyson markets the competing Dyson Airstrait, a hair dryer and straightener that uses directed airflow rather than heated plates. Dyson challenged claims comparing the SilkiPro to the Airstrait, as well as monadic claims about the SilkiPro’s performance.

“More Features”

The claim “More Features Half the Price” appeared in a comparative video. The National Advertising Division (NAD) found that the claim conveys that the Airstrait has fewer features overall than the SilkiPro and that Shark supported it. Though there were different ways to count the features, the SilkiPro had more under each count.

Because the margin depends on how features are enumerated, and consumers cannot evaluate the comparison without knowing the features counted, NAD recommended that, if Shark continues to make the claim, it clearly and conspicuously identify the features from both products being compared.

“When Air Just Isn’t Enough”

Dyson challenged a Shark video’s closing tagline, “When Air Just Isn’t Enough,” as suggesting that the Airstrait lacks benefits Shark associates with its combs. Shark agreed to permanently discontinue any message that the Airstrait does not effectively smooth, stretch and straighten hair, and indicated that it has discontinued the video. NAD found that the tagline, standing alone, does not convey an objective or comparative message about the Airstrait.

Consumer Reviews

Dyson challenged two reviews in the customer review section of the SilkiPro product page: “Drying and straightening in one step,” and “Perfect if you need to dry your hair quickly and get it straight all in one step.”

NAD found Shark responsible for the reposted, incentivized reviews and determined that they reasonably convey that a user can dry and straighten wet hair in one step, a message that NAD found to be unsupported. Accordingly, NAD recommended that Shark discontinue the two reviews.

During the inquiry, Shark voluntarily agreed to permanently discontinue a number of challenged express and implied product performance and comparative claims. NAD did not review these claims on the merits and will treat the permanently discontinued claims, for compliance purposes, as though NAD recommended they be discontinued.

In its advertiser statement, Shark stated that it “will comply with NAD’s decision and recommendation.”

data.title: GRIT Infrastructure Acquires Reinhard Boring Technologies
data.description:
GRIT Infrastructure announces the acquisition of Ohio-based horizontal auger boring firm Reinhard Boring Technologies, expanding its Midwest services to include in-house Jack and Bore capabilities. Effective November 20, 2026, Reinhard will operate as Reinhard Boring, LLC, a GRIT Infrastructure company.

COLUMBUS, Ohio--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- GRIT Infrastructure (GRIT), a portfolio company of MFG Partners, announced the acquisition of Reinhard Boring Technologies, a provider of horizontal auger boring for essential infrastructure utility services. This strategic acquisition marks an important expansion of GRIT’s Midwest in-house services offering and reinforces its commitment to partnering with high quality, client-focused utility service providers throughout the Midwest. Reinhard and GRIT will meld horizontal auger boring to the horizontal directional drilling and excavation work GRIT crews already perform across the Midwest, to offer a one stop shop to clients that need casing under roads, rail lines, and waterways all under one contract.

“We are very pleased to be joining forces with the team at Reinhard,” said Randall P. Muench, Chief Executive Officer of GRIT Infrastructure. “Clients have been asking us to expand to Jack C Bore services. Reinhard brings high-quality services and Danny and the Reinhard team are a great fit in our culture. We are so pleased to be adding them to the team.”

“GRIT gives us the reach and access to capital to grow faster than we ever could on our own. Both of our client bases will leverage the expertise we each bring to the underground utility market,” said Daniel Smith, owner and President of Reinhard. “This combination is a great fit for our people and our customers.”

Reinhard owner Daniel Smith will remain with the company as the leader of the jack and bore operation. The team will continue to operate out of the firm’s Troy, OH office and yard.

About GRIT Infrastructure

GRIT Infrastructure, headquartered in Grove City, Ohio, installs, repairs and maintains underground water, sewer, power, and gas utilities for commercial, municipal, utility and general contracting customers across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and Pennsylvania. Services include horizontal directional drilling, excavation, hydrovac, septic, sewer, and drain service. GRIT Infrastructure is the parent company of Daystar Directional Drilling, CST Utilities, Precise Boring of Ohio and Chuck's Septic Tank, Sewer C Drain Cleaning, Learn more at www.gritinfrastructure.com.

Based in Troy, OH, Reinhard has been serving the Ohio and Indiana market, providing underground services with a specialty in Jack C Bore/Auger Boring. For more information, go to https://www.reinhardboring.com.

data.title: Anthropic Shares Retreat After Blockbuster Debut Amid AI Anxiety
data.description:
10:41 AM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Anthropic's (ANT) shares slid on Friday, partially reversing gains from its blockbuster market debut amid mounting skepticism on Wall Street around stocks linked to artificial intelligence.

Shares of the Claude AI chatbot maker were most recently down 11%, having surged 17% in the previous session following a record listing.

Investors pulled back from other tech stocks too as they considered the durability of the AI boom amid soaring valuations. Major chipmakers such as Nvidia ( NVDA ) , Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) , Qualcomm ( QCOM ) , Micron Technology ( MU ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) all declined intraday Friday.

Anthropic's trading debut has failed to lift sentiment on Wall Street, which tumbled Thursday. The Nasdaq Composite was down 2% intraday Friday.

"We are concerned about Anthropic's revenue growth," Seaport Research Partners said in a Thursday note. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years."

Anthropic's sequential revenue growth fell to 43% in the third quarter from 144% in the second quarter, Seaport Senior Analyst Jay Goldberg wrote. "We acknowledge those are incredible growth rates in absolute terms, but the decline is worrying," he said.

Seaport assigned a neutral rating to Anthropic's stock.

"If Anthropic really is the greatest company ever, there will be time to buy later," the brokerage said.

"We are cautious, not negative."

Anthropic said Friday that it completed its upsized IPO, raising a total of about $93.5 billion. It sold about 1.13 billion common shares, including underwriters' full exercise of the overallotment option, at $83 apiece, above the marketed range.

Of the total share count, stockholders sold about 23.6 million shares.

Anthropic said it raised about $26 billion in a private placement from Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), Alphabet's (GOOGL, GOOG) Google ( GOOG ), Micron, Microsoft ( MSFT ) , Nvidia ( NVDA ) and TSMC Partners.

While Anthropic could establish a durable position in enterprise AI, there are multiple risks regarding owning the stock, including intensifying competition and massive infrastructure commitments, Saxo Bank said in a note on Friday.

"AI demand is booming, but intensifying competition and falling token prices could make it harder for Anthropic to turn growth into sustainable profits," Saxo Chief Investment Strategist Charu Chanana wrote.

data.title: Boeing leaves open possibility of more layoffs amid stalled production plans
data.description:
SEATTLE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - When pressed by one of its largest unions, Boeing ( BA ) management declined to say on Thursday if the company plans on further layoffs after an upcoming round next month.

"We asked if December 9 was the only date for (layoff notices) and were told Boeing ( BA ) didn't know," Bryan Corliss, a spokesman for the Society of Engineering Employees in Aerospace, told Reuters.

In early November, Boeing ( BA ) announced plans to cut 5% of the company's commercial airplanes division's roughly 50,000 employees through attrition and layoffs. The cuts were needed because it is taking longer than expected for the company to increase output of its 737 MAX jet, its largest moneymaker, the division's CEO Stephanie Pope explained in a memo to employees at the time.

Asked about SPEEA's comment, a Boeing ( BA ) spokesperson told Reuters, "We continue to work through an established process to ensure our workforce can support our customer commitments. We are committed to treating everyone with dignity and respect and will communicate details with impacted employees once decisions are finalized."

The company is trying to increase 737 production rate from 42 jets a month to 47, which it had planned to reach this past summer. Last month, Boeing ( BA ) CEO Kelly Ortberg told investors that the company now expects to reach that target in early 2027.

On Thursday, SPEEA told its roughly 17,000 members that Boeing ( BA ) managers told union officials that: 

"Employment at all Boeing Commercial Airplanes sites is under review, but layoffs won't necessarily impact all sites.

"These will not be across-the-board layoffs, but rather targeted layoffs focused on which work statements are ending or can be ended.

"There will be no voluntary layoffs or buy-outs."

SPEEA members approved a new four-year contract with the company in early October. Boeing ( BA ) managers told the union that the cuts were not retaliation for the contract, which included a guaranteed 10% wage increase ​upon ratification, along with ⁠annual raises of 4% and the possibility of an additional 2% pay hike based on performance.

(Reporting by Dan Catchpole in Seattle, Editing by Nick Zieminski)

data.title: US STOCKS-Nasdaq falls as Anthropic fails to rekindle AI optimism
data.description:
* Indexes: Dow up 0.7%, S&P 500 flat, Nasdaq down 0.51%

* Anthropic down 6% a day after debut

* Intuit down after company cuts revenue forecast, agrees to sell unit

(Updates after markets open, adds analyst comments)

By Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur

Nov 20 (Reuters) - The tech-heavy Nasdaq slid on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, undermining hopes that the listing would stabilize an AI trade already shaken by valuation concerns.

Anthropic shares fell 6% after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut.

The AI lab's IPO and Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings this week were seen as key tests of whether battered investor confidence in the AI trade could recover.

But neither revived enthusiasm after weeks of concern about the profitability of massive AI infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, regulatory risks following Democrats' win in the US midterm elections, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's departure.

The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

"The capex expansion is becoming too much, and people are asking how it's being funded. Is it coming from the core business, or is it increasingly funded by debt?" said Sadiq Adatia, chief investment officer at BMO Global Asset Management.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon ( AMZN ) was down 0.5% and Meta declined 2.6%, while Alphabet gained 2.3%. Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell 3.7%, with shares in the chipmaker hitting their lowest since June 2025 and heading for their longest weekly losing streak since 2008.

Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), Marvell ( MRVL ) , and Micron lost between 2% and 5.7%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3%.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius also dropped about 5% each.

Most of the major S&P 500 sectors were higher. Still, a 2% fall in the heavyweight technology group weighed on the market.

Healthcare stocks were up after four straight sessions of losses, also helping the Dow stay in positive territory.

At 9:56 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 353.84 points, or 0.70%, to 49,450.90, the S&P 500 gained 2.76 points, or 0.04%, to 7,178.59 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 121.36 points, or 0.51%, to 23,757.84.

The selloff in AI-linked stocks has largely overshadowed a strong earnings season.

Of the 462 companies in the S&P 500 to have reported results through Wednesday, 83.5% beat analyst earnings expectations, according to an analysis from Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed would need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high.

Markets are pricing in a 98.2% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Attention will also be on Fed Governor Lisa Cook's speech, expected later in the day.

A final University of Michigan survey showed consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 in November from 48.0 in October.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 3.6% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.05-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, and by a 1.22-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 11 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 9 new highs and 407 new lows.

data.title: Ezee Fiber Wins Two 2026 Fierce Network Innovation Awards

HOUSTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ezee Fiber won two categories in the 2026 Fierce Network Innovation Awards, a leading telecommunications industry awards program. Its fiber-to-the-home expansion in Albuquerque and Santa Fe was named Broadband Build of the Year, and CEO Matt Marino was named Innovator of the Year.

The awards were announced and presented Nov. 19 during Broadband Nation Expo at the Hilton Riverside in New Orleans. The ceremony marked the first live, in-person presentation of the awards in the program's more than 15-year history.

New Mexico build recognized for measurable community impact

The Broadband Build of the Year category honors completed builds with measurable community results. At the end of 2022, only about 4% of Bernalillo County and 9% of Santa Fe County could buy fiber at home. Ezee Fiber's $250 million New Mexico expansion, announced in 2023, now offers symmetrical residential speeds up to 8 Gbps and enterprise connectivity up to 400 Gbps, with no data caps.

A July 2026 Ezee Fiber-sponsored study by Dr. Brian Whitacre of Oklahoma State University ties roughly 661 local jobs to the rollout from 2021 to 2024 and estimates $77 million in home-value gains through 2025. More than 95% of the company's New Mexico roles are filled locally, and it has invested $98 million in in-state supply chain spending.

After a 2025 stop-work order in Albuquerque, Ezee Fiber worked with city leaders on "neighbor-first" construction protocols that cut construction-related 311 calls by 47% year over year.

"This award belongs to our New Mexico team," said Pedro Checo, chief operating officer of Ezee Fiber. "New Mexico shows what fiber can do when it's built with local people, local partners and a long-term commitment to the community."

Marino named Innovator of the Year

Since joining as CEO in 2023, Marino has built Ezee Fiber around the customer experience, pairing fast, reliable fiber with 24/7 local customer service. Under his leadership, that model is expanding from Texas and New Mexico into Washington, Illinois, Oregon and Michigan.

"Together, these awards recognize the commitment of our teams to building better networks, delivering exceptional service and earning the trust of customers and communities," Marino said. "Innovation is not simply about technology. It is about how effectively we deliver on our promises, solve problems and create lasting value for the people we serve."

The recognition marks the inaugural presentation of Fierce Network's Innovator of the Year award and highlights the growing influence of emerging fiber providers in an industry historically dominated by much larger companies.

Hiring and recognition continue as the industry contracts

Fierce Network honors add to a growing list of national industry recognitions for Ezee Fiber. PCMag named the company the best overall internet service provider in the U.S. for 2026 and included it among the Best Gaming ISPs (2025, 2026) and Fastest ISPs in the U.S. (2024, 2025).

Ezee Fiber has also earned 65 Speedtest by Ookla awards. A recent edition of Consumer Reports ranked Ezee Fiber among the nation's top 10 internet providers, with consumers praising its value, pricing and simplicity.

The recognition comes as Ezee Fiber continues to expand its network, customer base and workforce across six states. While several major U.S. telecommunications companies have announced substantial workforce reductions, Ezee Fiber continues to invest in new markets and hire employees in sales, field operations, customer service and other functions. The company employs approximately 800 people and is targeting 200,000 customers and 800,000 homes passed by the end of 2026.

Ezee Fiber's industry-leading speeds, award-winning customer service and transparent pricing model set the company apart. Learn more at www.ezeefiber.com.

data.title: GRAPHIC-The snowballing selloff in global markets
data.description:
LONDON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - A global financial market rout has taken a major turn for the worse this week as a noxious combination of worries over AI and US interest rates triggered an avalanche of selling from stocks to copper and gold.

1/STOCKS SHOCK

Nerves about a possible bubble in AI and tech stocks started to emerge around the middle of the year. But the selloff really started to snowball last month when it became clear that major economies such as the US would need further interest rate hikes to tame inflation.

Some of the milestones are eye-popping.

Nearly $9 trillion has been wiped off the value of world stocks since they peaked back in August while this week's 17% plunge in Taiwan is the biggest since the early 1990s.

Adding to the worries was this month's hammering of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party, which has cast doubts on how many US data centres will get built. The sudden resignation of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang also rattled investors given the key role the chip company plays in bankrolling the AI industry.

"What concerns me isn't so much the correction in technology stocks... but the possibility of the selling spreading into broader financial markets," said Bruno Schneller, managing director at Erlen Capital Management.

"Even gold has come under pressure, which is interesting given its traditional safe-haven role and may point to investors raising cash rather than simply rotating into defensive assets."

2/TURN UP THE VOL

Wall Street's fear gauge, ​the VIX index of US stock market volatility, reached 30 points on Friday, its highest since late March, as investors rushed to buy protection against market swings.

While the jump isn't yet at the scale of its post-April 2025 "Liberation Day" move, it's getting close and is now at a level that could trigger selling by hedge funds that target fixed levels of volatility.

The European equivalent of the VIX has also hit its highest level since April although other gauges suggest the stress, for now at least, isn't spreading.

The MOVE index, which tracks volatility ​in the US Treasury bond market, remains below last month's highs, as do implied volatility gauges for major currency pairs.

3/COPPER, OIL

The standout mover in metals is copper. A beneficiary of the AI rollout, given high demand for the metal from data centres, it is on course for its steepest weekly drop since April 2025.

Oil, which has been central to this year's inflation worries given how much higher prices have pushed up costs, has taken a back seat in the broader market drama of the last few days, staying in a relatively tight $90-$94 range.

4/BONDS, GOLD

Government bonds are performing well as a safe haven in this latest market turmoil, shrugging off worries about a more aggressive Federal Reserve.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield is on track for its biggest weekly fall since April 2025, down 17 basis points so far this week.

Bond yields move inversely to prices.

In Europe, the 10-year German Bund yield is down around 9 bps on Friday alone.

Analysts at Citi said the market could price out US rate hikes, lifting bonds, "if the US equity sell-off should morph into a bursting of the AI bubble."

Gold, however, is failing to play its safe-haven role, down around 1% on Friday to the lowest since September 2025.

5/DOLLAR WRECKING BALL

The dollar has shown that reports of its demise have been greatly exaggerated.

The greenback index, which measures the world's reserve currency against the six other top currencies, has risen to a 19-month high this week.

For the year it is nearly 7% higher against the euro, 3% up on the yen and between 4% and 5% stronger against sterling and the Canadian and kiwi dollars.

Emerging market currencies have been hit too. The added turbulence of a surprise election result has seen Brazil's currency slump more than 8% this month, while Israel's shekel, one of the currencies most correlated with the AI boom, has tumbled almost 5%.

(Reporting by Marc Jones and Alun John, additional reporting by Harry Robertson)

data.title: E-Power’s Joint Venture Designated a National-Level “Little Giant” Enterprise by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
data.description:
DOVER, USA, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- E-Power Inc. ( EPOW ) (“E-Power,” the “Company,” “we” or “our”) , a provider of advanced battery materials and AI Data Center (AIDC) microgrid solutions, today announced that its joint venture, Sunrise (Guizhou) New Energy Materials Co., Ltd. (“Sunrise Guizhou”), has been designated a national-level Specialized, Refined, Distinctive and Innovative (“Little Giant”) enterprise by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (“MIIT”) as part of the MIIT’s eighth batch of Little Giant designations. Sunrise Guizhou received notice of the designation on October 14, 2026 through the MIIT’s High-Quality SME Gradient Cultivation Platform.

The designation completes the national review process described in the Company’s press release of August 20, 2026, which announced that Sunrise Guizhou had passed provincial review by the Department of Industry and Information Technology of Guizhou Province and was one of 28 enterprises included in the province’s recommendation list for the eighth batch.

The Top Tier of China’s SME Cultivation System

The MIIT’s gradient cultivation system for high-quality small and medium-sized enterprises (“SMEs”) has three tiers: technology-based and innovative SMEs; specialized and sophisticated SMEs, recognized at the provincial level; and Little Giant enterprises, designated at the national level by the MIIT. Only enterprises that already hold provincial specialized and sophisticated SME status may apply for Little Giant designation. The program recognizes SMEs that focus on specific market segments, possess core technologies and strong innovation capabilities, and hold leading positions in their segments.

Applications for the eighth batch were assessed under the MIIT’s revised Measures for the Administration of Gradient Cultivation of High-Quality Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises, issued in January 2026. According to the MIIT’s notice to Sunrise Guizhou, the designation followed preliminary review and recommendation by local authorities, expert review, and internal deliberation by the MIIT. The MIIT’s review uses staged review, random assignment of experts and review tasks, and blind review, and cross-checks application data using data analysis tools. The designation is valid for three years, from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2029.

Progression Through All Three Tiers

Sunrise Guizhou has advanced through each tier of the system. It was recognized as an innovative SME in April 2023 and as a specialized and sophisticated SME in July 2024, and in May 2025 it was designated a Guizhou Province Key Specialized and Sophisticated SME. The Little Giant designation places it in the system’s top tier.

Sunrise Guizhou manufactures graphite anode materials and develops next-generation anode materials, including silicon-carbon composites and hard carbon for sodium-ion batteries. It was certified as a National High-Tech Enterprise in 2023. In 2024, one of its projects was selected through the “Open Competition” (Jie Bang Gua Shuai) mechanism of an MIIT industrial foundation innovation program and passed final acceptance in December 2024. In May 2025, it received an Excellence Award at the 25th China Patent Awards, granted by the China National Intellectual Property Administration, and in 2026 it participated in drafting the national standard “Porous Carbon for Silicon-Based Anode Materials” .

“This designation completes the national review that followed Guizhou’s provincial recommendation earlier this year, and we see it as recognition of our Guizhou team’s long-standing focus on anode materials,” said Mr. Haiping Hu, the founder, CEO and Chairman of E-Power Inc. ( EPOW ) “Because the designation is reviewed every three years, we intend to keep earning it through continued investment in research, standards work and manufacturing quality.”

E-Power Inc. ( EPOW ), through its subsidiaries, joint venture and variable interest entity structure, is engaged in the manufacturing and sale of graphite anode material for lithium-ion batteries. Through its joint venture, the Company operates a plant in Guizhou Province, China, powered by electricity from renewable sources, which contributes to the plant’s competitive production costs and reduced environmental impact in the production of graphite anode material. data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Robinhood faces shareholder challenge as SEC loosens proxy oversight
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - A shareholder activist group called for online brokerage Robinhood to review its proxy-voting platform, concerned that retail investors aren't getting fair choices as financial regulators weaken balloting rules for corporate annual meetings.

Robinhood and its Say investor-communications arm are at the center of changes coming to contests like director elections or CEO pay approvals. Robinhood worked with Tesla to create a way for retail investors to cast their ballots automatically that won approval from the US Securities and Exchange Commission in September.

Backers say such retail-voting plans will increase retail investors' voting participation rates, even as the SEC takes steps that could eliminate shareholder proposals at corporate meetings. Critics say Tesla and others like ExxonMobil are designing their programs to unfairly channel votes in favor of management recommendations.

A shareholder resolution filed with Robinhood for its next annual meeting, seen by Reuters, could spark debate about the role of investor rights. In the resolution the activist group As You Sow says Robinhood limits customers to using its own voting platform that requires a "painstaking and time-consuming challenge" to vote on individual corporate ballot items, rather than using third-party voting services.

It also notes Robinhood's work with Tesla's management-friendly voting option. The limited voting choices create legal and reputational risks, said As You Sow in its resolution, which calls for Robinhood to review offering clients more ways to vote, "including an independent voting service of their choice."

As You Sow leaders said ideally Robinhood might offer something like Vanguard's voting program which casts prorated shares of funds' votes according to investors' preferences. Vanguard clients can select among voting policies like one that tends to support environmental and social shareholder resolutions, or one that supports management recommendations.

Robinhood "shouldn't be limiting choices," said Danielle Fugere, As You Sow president, in an interview. "You should get to choose. That's what voting is all about."

Robinhood representatives did not respond to messages seeking comment.

(Reporting by Ross Kerber; Editing by Sonali Paul)

data.title: SpaceX's Cursor weighs phasing out Chinese AI models over geopolitical risk, CNBC reports
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - SpaceX's AI coding platform, Cursor, is considering moving away from Chinese AI models due to "geopolitical risk," CNBC reported on Friday, citing a report by the House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Select Committee on China.

The report, which follows a months-long investigation into the adoption of Chinese AI models into the American tech stack, said Cursor "informed the committees" of those plans. Vacation-rental firm Airbnb and food delivery firm DoorDash also engaged with the investigation about their use of Chinese AI models, according to CNBC.

SpaceX, Cursor, Airbnb, DoorDash and the congressional committees did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

Reuters exclusively reported earlier this week that the Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, a bid to discourage reliance on the technology without imposing new restrictions that could anger industry or Beijing.

The Treasury Department and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy have discussed the plan, which would apply to companies such as Airbnb, Reuters has reported.

Earlier this year, SpaceX acquired the startup behind Cursor, Anysphere, in a $60 billion all-stock deal to boost its presence in the lucrative enterprise AI tools market.

SpaceX is developing its Grok family of AI models in collaboration with Cursor, which has been involved in their training.

data.title: Anthropic's post-debut stumble delivers reality check for AI trade
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Anthropic's post-listing slide deepened the gloom over the AI sector on Friday, underscoring how even one of the most eagerly anticipated listings in history has struggled to revive investor enthusiasm.

Widely seen as a proxy for the AI trade, Anthropic's listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain momentum after a turbulent stretch.

But the stock was last trading at $88.25, about 9% below where it closed following Thursday's smooth debut, giving Anthropic a fully diluted valuation of about $1.6 trillion and a market capitalization of about $1.2 trillion based on shares outstanding.

The stock could find support later in the year. London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates index-tracking funds could account for purchases of up to 30% of Anthropic's shares by year-end.

Near-term volatility, however, could persist as the initial euphoria around the listing fades and investors assess whether a valuation of about 40 times sales over the past 12 months can be sustained.

"We favor patience on Anthropic and recommend evaluating the company as it reports public results," said Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at US Bank Asset Management, adding that the current valuation "assumes years of rapid growth."

The debut has also done little to ease broader concerns about the health of the AI trade. Wall Street's main indexes ended sharply lower on Thursday, while futures pointed to further declines on Friday.

Among the Magnificent Seven stocks, Nvidia and Meta Platforms fell more than 3% each in premarket trading, while Amazon and Microsoft dropped more than 2%.

Chip stocks also slid, with AMD and Sandisk down over 6% each and Intel losing more than 4%.

The focus now shifts to a potential OpenAI listing, which would be another major test of investors' appetite for AI stocks. OpenAI has indicated it may go public next year.

PARALLELS WITH SPACEX

Anthropic's IPO has drawn parallels with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which went public in June after the second-biggest IPO on record.

Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its IPO after underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares, surpassing SpaceX's $85.7 billion haul to become the biggest listing on record.

While the companies have different business models, some investors have pointed to SpaceX's sharp swings in the weeks after its debut as a reason for caution over buying Anthropic immediately after its listing.

"There's going to be some volatility like we had with SpaceX. A lot of people are going to have FOMO. I don't think there's any need to get on it on the first trade," said Rob Hackel, CEO of financial advisory and brokerage firm RF Lafferty & Co.

SpaceX shares fell about 6%.

Retail investors traded about $772 million of Anthropic shares on Thursday, the most for an IPO debut since Vanda Research began tracking the data in 2012.

The stock's sharp swings have left investors weighing whether to bet on a rebound or brace for further losses. Options trading, due to begin next week, could add to the volatility.

"It's not a good environment for Anthropic at the moment," said Carsten Hesse, head of index events at Berenberg.

Competition could also weigh on investor sentiment.

Apple is developing an AI agent that can perform tasks on behalf of users, entering a market already being pursued by OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, Bloomberg News reported on Friday.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant in Bengaluru and Vidya Ranganathan in London; Editing by Anil D'Silva)

data.title: HireClix Introduces Verified Apply for Career Sites, Integrating Human Verification in the Application Process to Improve the Quality of Applicants
data.description:
HireClix Career Site adds new security solution to core platform functionality and introduces a human check between “Apply” and employers’ ATS, combating fraudulent job applications without added friction to the candidate experience

GLOUCESTER, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- HireClix, a leading recruitment marketing services company, today announced a significant enhancement to its Career Site platform in the form of its new Verified Apply solution. The solution is a one-second human check that filters out automated noise, protecting candidate quality and saving on recruiter time, while keeping the candidate experience fast, familiar and welcoming for human candidates. Verified Apply adds a brief, invisible-by-design human check at the exact moment a candidate clicks Apply, allowing candidates to complete a near-instant verification and continue straight into the application experience.

Career sites are increasingly under pressure by non-human traffic (NHT) or automated bot traffic – from automation that can cause havoc on the site all the way into the candidate application pool. This enhancement will upgrade the quality of the job seekers by setting a roadblock for spam apply engines and many bad actors. When these types of aggressive tactics are used they show up in the form of hundreds or thousands of applications. Such a glut of candidates wastes significant recruiter time, sorting through low-quality or fraudulent submissions, while real candidates are buried in the pile. Verified Apply is powered by Cloudflare Turnstile, the same technology trusted by many of the web's largest platforms. Rather than asking candidates to prove they're human by solving a puzzle, it quietly confirms that a real browser, on a real device, is making the request. Verification is confirmed before the candidate is ever handed off to an employer’s applicant tracking system, so a passing result can be verified as a human.

“Everyone knows that all bad actors can’t be stopped, but adding Verified Apply to the HireClix Career Site Solution solves many of the challenges in today’s recruiting world faced by all employers from enterprise to the mid-market. Leveraging Cloudflare Turnstile for our solution enables us to utilize the best of the technology in the consumer marketplace and apply it to our client’s recruiting challenges,” said Neil Costa, CEO and Founder of HireClix. “We continue to invest in a career site solution that improves the candidate experience while also serving the client’s needs to get better quality applicants so they can fill their open roles.”

The Verified Apply solution serves as a frictionless alternative to other forms of verification, reducing scripted, bulk and fraudulent applications before they reach the ATS, thus saving recruiter time spent reviewing mismatched or low-quality applications.

On the candidate side, the experience is designed to be fast and unobtrusive:

  • A candidate clicks Apply on the careers site job detail page.
  • A branded, on-page verification appears as Verified Apply activates.
  • Most candidates pass with little or no interaction – Cloudflare Turnstile often confirms they are human without extra steps.
  • The candidate continues directly into the existing application process.

Verified Apply is also built to protect candidate privacy. It does not collect resumes, names, or application answers; it does not change or replace the existing application system; and it does not share traffic or configuration across clients. Any handoff data (such as the approved Apply destination, optional job ID, and attribution parameters) is short-lived and used only to complete the verification step. Every client runs on its own dedicated, isolated verification configuration – nothing is pooled or shared. Employers can keep existing analytics and reporting in place.

“The future of recruiting is not about generating the highest number of applications, but rather giving recruiters the tools needed to ensure they can meaningfully engage with high-quality candidates,” added Costa. “Verified Apply allows employers to preserve the candidate experience, a consistent and fully branded career site, reduce bulk and automated bots to mitigate risk, all while protecting the employer’s resources and recruiters’ time.”

To learn more about HireClix’s Verified Apply solution visit: https://www.hireclix.com/recruitment-marketing/career-site-solutions-verified-apply

About HireClix

HireClix is a recruitment marketing agency that provides full agency of record and strategic talent acquisition services to help clients achieve their recruiting and employer branding goals. HireClix also provides full career site creative design and development services on a state-of-the-art and secure content management system for employers, leading to enhancements in the candidate experience, placement within search engines and AI agents and improved overall employer branding. HireClix’s recruitment advertising agency services include programmatic job board media buying and the HireClix Employer Brand Network, by targeting key audiences so employers can reach passive candidates on consumer sites. In addition, the HireClix Advanced Analytics Dashboard (HAAD) blends advertising metrics, career site analytics and data from any ATS to give visibility to quality applications and cost per hire. HireClix was founded in 2010 with a focus on helping clients get the best overall return on investment for their recruiting dollars and continues to be the fastest-growing recruitment advertising agency in the industry, advertising in 40+ countries around the globe for a diverse group of enterprise clients. data.title: MTI Aviation Appoints Tony DiSimone Sr. and Aviv Tzur to Board of Directors

OKLAHOMA CITY and OPA-LOCKA, Fla., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MTI Aviation ("MTI"), an Acorn Company, a leading provider of repair, overhaul and parts distribution services, with a primary focus on electro-mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and power generation components, today announced the appointment of Tony DiSimone Sr. and Aviv Tzur to its Board of Directors. Both are accomplished aviation entrepreneurs who bring decades of experience in building companies in the aviation aftermarket, strengthening MTI's board following its majority investment by Acorn Capital Management ("Acorn") earlier this year.

Jorge Mejia, CEO of MTI, stated, "Tony and Aviv have each built successful aviation businesses from the ground up. Their experience and judgment will be invaluable as we execute on the growth plan we have established with Acorn which includes expansion of our capabilities, as well as acquiring other Part 145 repair stations."

Tony DiSimone Sr. founded Sentry Aerospace in 1975 and today serves as Executive Chairman of Sentry Aerospares ("Sentry"), an Acorn company, following its merger with Aerospares 2000 in July 2022. During this time, Mr. DiSimone helped Sentry to firmly entrench its leadership position in the Aircraft-on-Ground spare parts market and help guide its global expansion.

"After more than five decades in the aviation aftermarket, MTI is one of the most impressive repair and overhaul operations that I have ever seen. I look forward to my experience, relationships, and guidance being additive to the outstanding business that Jorge has built," said Mr. DiSimone.

Aviv Tzur is the founder of Avbiz Aerospace Ventures, which he established in 2002 as a platform for capital investment in aviation companies. Mr. Tzur previously served as CEO of Avborne Heavy Maintenance (now AAR Miami), which is today one of the largest aircraft heavy maintenance operations in Florida. Currently, Mr. Tzur serves as President of the Greater Miami Aviation Association and is a founding director of the aviation finance program at the University of Miami's business school. Mr. Tzur also currently serves on the Board of Directors of Sentry.

"Having spent my career on both the operational and finance sides of aviation, I'm excited to help guide MTI through the next phase of its growth. Jorge has built an outstanding business with enormous opportunities ahead following MTI's partnership with Acorn," said Mr. Tzur.

Greg Agnew, a Partner at Acorn, commented, "We are excited to welcome Tony and Aviv to MTI's Board of Directors, as both are proven winners and will be instrumental in furthering MTI's growth and elevating its already strong position in the aviation aftermarket."
